chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about eating raw meat, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is the food of wild animals'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating raw meat in Shia Islam according to Hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) characterizes raw meat (*ni'j*) as the food of wild beasts (*siba'*), reflecting the Shia scholarly view that while not necessarily forbidden, it is culturally and physically inferior for humans. This classification aligns with the concept of *karahat* (dislike) rather than *haram*, emphasizing the refinement of human consumption compared to animals. The narration highlights the importance of *adab* (etiquette) in eating, distinguishing human dietary habits from those of beasts of prey.
